mainTopic: Walled cities from יהושע's time, רבי יהושע בן לוי's rulings on reading the מגילה, and why villages may read early
overview: This amud finishes רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement that לוד, אונו, and גיא החרשים have been walled since the days of יהושע בן נון. The גמרא asks how that can be, since verses say that אלפעל and later אסא built these cities. רבי אלעזר explains the history: the cities were walled in יהושע's time, destroyed in the war of פילגש בגבעה, rebuilt by אלפעל, and restored by אסא. The wording of אסא's verse, 'these cities', supports this. Next come more rulings of רבי יהושע בן לוי. Women are obligated in מקרא מגילה because they were part of the miracle. When פורים falls on שבת, people still learn its laws, and this is allowed despite רבה's גזירה. The מגילה must also be read at night and again by day, which רבי ירמיה and עולא ביראה confirm. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה, and רבי חנינא explains why villages may read early on יום הכניסה.

steps.title: Three cities walled since the time of יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement (begun on the previous amud) is that לוד, אונו, and גיא החרשים have been walled since the days of יהושע בן נון.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוד, אונו, and גיא החרשים are cities that have had walls around them since the days of יהושע בן נון.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a statement by רבי יהושע בן לוי that begins on the previous amud. He names three cities that count as מוקפות חומה מימות יהושע בן נון, meaning they have been walled since יהושע's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being walled since יהושע's time is the key test for reading the מגילה on the fifteenth of אדר (שושן פורים). So the גמרא is giving a practical fact: these three cities fall into the walled-city category.

keyTerms.meaning: Since the days of Joshua son of Nun
Gei HaCharashim, 'Valley of the Craftsmen', a city name

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether a city was walled in יהושע's time decides if it reads the מגילה on the 14th or the 15th of אדר.

phrases.english: Lod, and Ono, and Gei HaCharashim

phrases.aramaic: מוּקָּפוֹת חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן הֲווֹ.
phrases.english: were surrounded by a wall since the days of Joshua son of Nun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of these specific cities.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוד, אונו, and גיא החרשים have the status of cities walled since the days of יהושע בן נון.

steps.title: Challenge: a verse says אלפעל built these cities
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how יהושע could have built these cities when a verse in דברי הימים says אלפעל's descendants built אונו and לוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did יהושע build these cities? Didn't אלפעל build them? As it is written: 'And the sons of אלפעל: עבר, and משעם, and שמר, who built אונו and לוד with its villages.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim from Step 1. It points to a verse saying אלפעל's family built אונו and לוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלפעל lived long after יהושע. If אלפעל built these cities, it looks like they did not exist, and were not walled, in יהושע's time.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: And did Joshua build these?
But Elpaal built them,
as it is written: 'And the sons of Elpaal:
Eber, and Misham, and Shemed,
he built Ono
and Lod with its villages'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּנַנְהִי? וְהָא אֶלְפַּעַל בְּנַנְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the historical claim of Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that these cities were walled since יהושע's time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse credits the later figure אלפעל with building them, which suggests they were founded after יהושע.

steps.title: Counter: by that logic אסא built them too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that another verse says אסא built the fortified cities of יהודה, so the word 'built' cannot prove a city was brand new.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, אסא built them too, as it is written: 'And אסא built fortified cities in יהודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge. If 'built' means 'founded for the first time,' then the verse about אסא would mean אסא founded these cities as well, which cannot be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different people are said to have 'built' the same cities, so 'built' must sometimes mean rebuilt or restored. That removes the proof from the אלפעל verse. Step 4 then explains how all of this fits together.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turns the challenger's logic back on him)

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say אסא founded these cities. It shows that the challenger's reading would lead to an impossible result, so 'built' cannot mean 'founded.'

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, Asa built them,
as it is written: 'And Asa built
the fortified cities that belong to Judah.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof used in Step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from the אלפעל verse. It does not yet give a full positive explanation.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumes 'built' means 'founded for the first time.' A second verse shows the same cities were 'built' again by אסא, so that assumption fails.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's history: walled, destroyed, rebuilt, restored
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the cities were walled in יהושע's time, destroyed in the war of פילגש בגבעה, rebuilt by אלפעל, fell again, and were restored by אסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: These cities were surrounded by walls since the days of יהושע בן נון. They were destroyed in the days of פילגש בגבעה, and אלפעל came and built them. They fell again, and אסא came and restored them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר settles the question by giving the cities' full timeline, so that all three sources fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original walled status from יהושע's time stays in place. אלפעל's building and אסא's building were later rebuildings after the cities were destroyed. Since לוד and אונו were in the land of בנימין, they were ruined in the war of פילגש בגבעה, when the cities of בנימין were destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: The concubine in Gibeah, the episode that led to the war against בנימין (שופטים יט–כא)

steps.whatToRemember: These cities keep their status of being walled since יהושע's time. אלפעל and אסא only rebuilt cities that had already been there.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
These were surrounded by a wall
since the days of Joshua son of Nun.
They were destroyed in the days of the concubine in Gibeah,
and Elpaal came and built them.
They fell again,
and Asa came and restored them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הָנֵי מוּקָּפוֹת חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the positive resolution that fits the claim in Step 1 with the verses in Steps 2 and 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical reconciliation: the cities were built several times.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the verse about אלפעל means the cities did not exist before him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cities were walled in יהושע's time. אלפעל rebuilt them after they were destroyed, and אסא restored them after they fell again.

steps.title: Proof from the wording of אסא's verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the verse about אסא says 'let us build these cities,' which means they were already cities before. This supports רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, as it is written: 'And he said to יהודה: Let us build these cities.' This shows that they were already cities at the start. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי אלעזר from the exact words of the verse about אסא, and then concludes 'שמע מינה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: אסא calls them 'these cities' before he builds them, so they already existed as cities. That shows his 'building' was a restoration, just as רבי אלעזר said.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise (supports the explanation)

steps.whatToRemember: The verse calls them 'these cities' before אסא builds them. This proves they already existed, which confirms רבי אלעזר's timeline.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
as it is written: 'And he said to Judah:
Let us build these cities,'
which implies that they were cities from the outset.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's resolution in Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's claim that אסא restored cities that already existed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב יד:ו, 'נבנה את הערים האלה,' which calls them 'these cities' before the building.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: לוד, אונו, and גיא החרשים are cities walled since the days of יהושע בן נון. Later 'building' by אלפעל and אסא was rebuilding and restoration.

steps.title: Women are obligated to hear the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that women are obligated in מקרא מגילה because they too were part of the פורים miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Women are obligated to read the מגילה, because they too were part of that miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ruling from רבי יהושע בן לוי. Women are obligated in מקרא מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is אף הן היו באותו הנס, meaning women were also part of the miracle. Since they were saved too, they share the duty to publicize it. This reason makes the obligation depend on being part of the miracle, not just on gender rules for time-bound מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: The reading of the מגילה (מגילת אסתר)
They too were part of that miracle

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for women's obligation in מקרא מגילה, even though women are usually exempt from מצוות עשה שהזמן גרמא. The same reason, אף הן היו באותו הנס, is used for other מצוות too.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Women are obligated in the reading of the Megillah,
for they too were part of that miracle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new series of teachings from רבי יהושע בן לוי. It is connected to the earlier steps only by the same speaker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are obligated in מקרא מגילה because they were part of the miracle.

steps.title: Learning the laws of פורים when it falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that when פורים falls on שבת, people ask and teach about the laws of the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: When פורים falls on שבת, people ask questions and teach about the topic of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives another ruling. When פורים falls on שבת, people should still ask about and teach the laws of פורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On such a שבת the מגילה itself is not read. Even so, the day's topic, פורים, should still be studied and taught. This ruling is about learning the laws, not about reading the מגילה.

keyTerms.meaning: That happens to fall on שבת
About the topic of the day

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
When Purim falls on Shabbat,
we ask and expound about the topic of the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling in the same series from רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When פורים falls on שבת, people ask about and teach the laws of פורים.

steps.title: Why single out פורים, when every holiday has this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהושע בן לוי needed to mention פורים, since a ברייתא says משה set up learning the laws of every holiday on that holiday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why mention פורים specifically? This is true even for a יום טוב! As a ברייתא teaches: משה set up for ישראל that they should ask and teach about the topic of the day: the laws of פסח on פסח, the laws of עצרת on עצרת, and the laws of סוכות on סוכות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last ruling. If learning the laws of every holiday on that holiday is already a known rule, why did רבי יהושע בן לוי need to say it about פורים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that משה set up a general rule: learn about each holiday on that holiday. If so, פורים seems to be covered already, and רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling looks unnecessary. The attack is not on the ruling's truth, but on why it needed to be said.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? (Why single it out?)

phrases.english: Why specifically Purim?
Even a Yom Tov too!
As it is taught: Moshe enacted for Israel

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהוּ שׁוֹאֲלִין וְדוֹרְשִׁין בְּעִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁל יוֹם:
phrases.english: that they should ask and expound about the topic of the day:
the laws of Pesach on Pesach,
the laws of Shavuot on Shavuot,
and the laws of Sukkot on Sukkot!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why the ruling in step 7 needed to be said.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling that people learn about פורים when it falls on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא already teaches that משה set up learning the laws of every holiday on that holiday, so mentioning פורים seems unnecessary.

steps.title: פורים needed to be mentioned because of רבה's decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought learning about פורים on שבת is forbidden because of רבה's גזירה, so רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: פורים needed to be mentioned. You might have said: Let us make a גזירה because of רבה's concern. So it teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. פורים on שבת is a special case, so it needed its own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה taught that the מגילה is not read on שבת. The concern is that someone might carry it in a public place to learn how to read it. We might have thought that teaching פורים's laws on that שבת should also be forbidden, since it might lead someone to read or carry the מגילה. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that we do not make that extra גזירה, and learning the laws is still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed for him (to say)
You might have said (a mistaken first thought)
Let us make a protective decree
It teaches us (that the first thought is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: The מגילה is still not read on שבת. This answer only allows learning and teaching the laws of פורים on that day, not reading the מגילה.
steps.whatToRemember: פורים on שבת needed its own ruling. Because of רבה's גזירה, we might have banned even learning about it. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that learning the laws is still allowed.

phrases.english: It was necessary for him to mention Purim,
lest you say: let us decree because of Rabba's concern,
phrases.notes: רבה: the מגילה is not read on שבת, lest one carry it four אמות in a public domain to learn from an expert.

phrases.english: so he teaches us that we do not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by showing what is new in the פורים ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows why the ruling was needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought that because of רבה's גזירה, even teaching פורים's laws on שבת should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not add that גזירה. Learning and teaching the laws of פורים on שבת is allowed.

steps.title: Reading the מגילה at night and again by day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a person must read the מגילה at night and again during the day, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A person must read the מגילה at night and repeat it during the day, as it says: 'My God, I call by day and You do not answer, and at night, and there is no silence for me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives another ruling about פורים. The מגילה must be read twice: once at night and once during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is a פסוק in תהלים that mentions calling out both by day (יומם) and by night (לילה). This hints at two readings of the מגילה. The word ולשנותה means to do it a second time, so the night reading comes first and the day reading repeats it.

keyTerms.meaning: And to repeat it (do it a second time)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of reading the מגילה twice on פורים: at night and again in the morning.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיב אָדָם לִקְרוֹת אֶת הַמְּגִילָּה בַּלַּיְלָה
phrases.english: A person is obligated to read the Megillah at night
and to repeat it during the day,
as it is said: 'My God, I call by day and You do not answer,
and at night, and there is no silence for me.' (Psalms 22:3)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling in the series from רבי יהושע בן לוי, starting a new point about when the מגילה is read.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מגילה must be read at night and again during the day, hinted at in תהלים כ״ב:ג׳.

steps.title: Some students misunderstand the word 'to repeat it'
steps.stepSummary: Some students understood רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling to mean: read the מגילה at night, and learn the משנה about it by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people understood from this ruling that one should read the מגילה at night and study its משנה by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how some students first read רבי יהושע בן לוי's words. This sets up the next step, where this reading will be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לשנותה' can mean 'to learn משנה,' because שנה is the root of משנה. So these students thought the daytime duty was to study the laws of the מגילה, not to read it a second time.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it (a first understanding that may later be rejected)
And to learn or study (from the root of משנה)
Its משנה, meaning the משניות dealing with the מגילה

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the final meaning. The word 'סבור מינה' is a signal that the גמרא is about to correct this understanding.

phrases.english: They understood from it
to read it at night
and to study its Mishnah by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first understanding of the word 'לשנותה' in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A proposed understanding (later rejected in step 12): read the מגילה at night, and study its משנה by day.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה explains that it means reading the מגילה again
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה rejects the students' reading. He heard directly from רבי חייא בר אבא that 'לשנותה' means to repeat the reading, just as people say 'I'll finish this section and go over it again.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to them: It was explained to me personally by רבי חייא בר אבא, like people say: 'I will finish this section and repeat it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה corrects the students. The daytime duty is to read the מגילה a second time, not to study its laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He proves this from everyday speech. People use 'אתנייה' to mean 'go over it again.' So 'לשנותה' means to repeat the same reading by day. He also has a direct tradition from רבי חייא בר אבא, who passed on רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: To me it was personally explained
And I will repeat or review it

steps.whatToRemember: 'לשנותה ביום' means reading the מגילה a second time during the day. It does not mean studying its משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה that we read the full מגילה twice on פורים, once at night and once by day.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to them:
To me it was explained
by Rabbi Chiya bar Abba himself,
like what people say:
I will finish this section and repeat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the understanding given in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that 'לשנותה' means learning the משנה about the מגילה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In ordinary speech, the word means repeating the same material. So the daytime duty is a second reading of the מגילה.

steps.title: Another אמורא says the same ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that עולא ביראה, quoted by רבי חלבו, also taught that one must read the מגילה at night and repeat it by day, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said: רבי חלבו said in the name of עולא ביראה: A person must read the מגילה at night and repeat it by day, as it says: 'So that my glory may sing to You and not be silent; ה' my God, I will thank You forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second אמורא who said the same ruling. This backs up רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'איתמר נמי' means 'it was also stated.' It shows that the ruling is not only רבי יהושע בן לוי's view. The פסוק has two parts: 'singing praise' and 'not being silent.' This hints at two readings, one at night and one by day.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (another אמורא says the same thing)
עולא from the place called בירה

phrases.english: It was also stated,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר עוּלָּא בִּירָאָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said that Ulla Bira'a said:

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיב אָדָם לִקְרוֹת אֶת הַמְּגִילָּה בַּלַּיְלָה
phrases.english: A person is obligated to read the Megillah at night
and to repeat it by day, as it is said:
"So that my glory may sing praise to You and not be silent,
phrases.notes: The two halves of this פסוק hint at the two readings.

phrases.english: O Lord my God, I will thank You forever."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the conclusion of step 12 by showing that another אמורא said the same ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the מגילה must be read at night and read again by day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parallel statement of עולא ביראה, quoted by רבי חלבו, based on תהלים 30:13.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the משנה about villages reading early
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which says that villages may move their reading earlier, to יום הכניסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: except that villages may read early, on the day of gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to start a new topic. This sets up the next step, where a reason is given for this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, unwalled towns read on the 14th of אדר. The משנה lets villages read earlier, on the Monday or Thursday before פורים. On those days villagers came to town for בית דין and קריאת התורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The day of gathering: Monday or Thursday, when villagers came to town

phrases.english: except that the villages may move their reading earlier
to the day of gathering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of night and day readings and returns to the משנה to discuss a new rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Villages may read the מגילה early, on יום הכניסה.

steps.title: Why villages were allowed to read early
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that חכמים were lenient with the villages so they would be free on פורים to bring water and food to their fellow Jews in the cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: The חכמים were lenient with the villages and let them read early on the day of gathering, so that they could supply water and food to their brothers in the cities.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives the reason behind the משנה's rule about villages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading early on יום הכניסה is a special leniency. It does not mean the 14th stops being the villagers' real day. Because they already read, the villagers are free on פורים to supply food and water to the city people. This way the city people can celebrate properly.
steps.whatToRemember: Villages may read early on יום הכניסה only because of a leniency of חכמים. The reason is to free them to supply food and water to the cities on פורים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
The Sages were lenient with the villages
to let them read earlier, on the day of gathering,
so that they could supply water and food
to their brothers in the cities.
